tx-harris-2026-county-judge-sanchez-orla.name: Orlando Sanchez
tx-harris-2026-county-judge-sanchez-orla.bio: Former Harris County Treasurer (12 years) and Houston City Council member (6 years); U.S. Air Force veteran.

positions.stance: Will focus county spending on core services, eliminate waste, and require every tax dollar to produce measurable results before asking taxpayers to pay more.
Will insist on measurable performance, open contracting and competitive bidding, responsible budgeting, independent audits, and clear consequences when projects fail.
Will focus on completing promised flood-control projects and working with neighboring counties on regional drainage, emergency planning, and infrastructure.
Will fully support the Sheriff's Office, Constables, prosecutors, and courts, improve staffing and response times, and publish public safety performance measures.
Says HISD's elected Trustees should begin rotating back onto the Board in a structured way that protects academic gains since the state takeover.

tx-harris-2026-county-judge-plummer-leti.name: Letitia Plummer
tx-harris-2026-county-judge-plummer-leti.bio: Dentist and small business owner of more than 25 years.

positions.stance: Supports funding an additional flood-control reservoir, winter weather preparedness, community resilience hubs, and expanded multilingual disaster education.
Would stop county property tax increases, increase support for first-time home buyers, and help small businesses through microlender partnerships and faster permits.
Proposes a preventive healthcare technology partnership, youth mental health partnerships with schools, countywide chronic illness education, and stronger environmental health standards.
Would introduce a "Justice to Workforce" model in county jails to reduce recidivism, fund crisis response, and defend immigrant rights.

tx-harris-2026-ccl-civil1-lopez-sonia.bio: Presiding judge of Harris County Civil Court at Law No. 1; former Associate General Counsel for the Lone Star College System.
